textRun.content: A Complete Compendium of American Disease Names, Clinical Counterparts, and Viral Chains
Introduction: The Architecture of the Chain
Every entry in this text runs through an unbroken historical and biological chain:
American name → disease → symptomology → bacteria → fungi / yeast / mold → immunoglobulins → serotyping → virus (the end)

The American name preserves the cultural and sensory experience of illness—what the patient felt, where it struck, or how it behaved. The Latin counterpart fixes the modern biological reality. Together, they map how folk memory connects to microscopic etiology.
= Working thesis / naming directive (Lou Gehrig’s disease framework)
= Unknown or empty record, kept open without invention

Fungi / Yeast / Mold / Immunoglobulins / Serotyping / Virus:
Fever lasting one day with intense sweating [D].
Convulsions of labor [D]. Cross-read: motor storms beside Lou Gehrig's motor erosion [LOGIC].
Homesickness historically listed as a fatal disease and cause of death [D]. Medicine dropped it rather than inventing a false mechanism.
All 53 entries successfully traced through the rigorous 8-point biological chain.
Viruses act as the small connecting nodes where folk names and Latin classifications meet, with bacteria, fungi, yeasts, and molds anchoring the intermediate pathology.
